candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the request URI (including percent-encoded characters such as %0a/%0d) and can therefore influence the servletPath/pathInfo values that RegexRequestMatcher concatenates and matches. The pattern itself is configured by the application.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that RegexRequestMatcher is used by the configuration layer (AbstractRequestMatcherRegistry.regexMatchers) and that no equivalent newline handling exists anywhere in the class: url is built verbatim from servletPath/pathInfo/queryString and matches() is a straight full-region regex match; the constructor compiles only CASE_INSENSITIVE. Verified the downstream decision path: DefaultFilterInvocationSecurityMetadataSource returns null when no matcher matches, and AbstractSecurityInterceptor explicitly skips authentication/authorization for null/empty attributes, with rejectPublicInvocations defaulting to false. Also checked alternatives: AntPathRequestMatcher (segment-based, no regex), MvcRequestMatcher (delegates to MVC/Ant) and DefaultHttpFirewall do not reject CR/LF in servletPath/pathInfo either, so they do not close this path. Counterevidence limiting the finding: servlet containers may reject or normalize encoded control characters, so the bypass requires a container/decoding combination that surfaces the line terminator to Java code; Java Matcher.matches() semantics with a trailing line terminator is reasoned from language behavior and was not executed (no runtime testing permitted), so the exact input needed was not verified at runtime.
candidates.impact: Potential bypass of URL-based authorization constraints (vertical/privilege separation loss) for applications that rely on regex request matchers, e.g. a non-privileged or unauthenticated user reaching a resource that a regex rule was intended to protect. No exploitation was attempted; impact is conditional on the prerequisites above.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) The application secures URLs using RegexRequestMatcher/regexMatchers() (not AntPathRequestMatcher) for the protected path; 2) the servlet container delivers a line terminator in the decoded servletPath/pathInfo (or query string) for a request that it still routes to the protected resource once normalized; 3) the protected rule is the only rule covering that path (no later matcher such as anyRequest().authenticated() catches the rewritten URL) and rejectPublicInvocations is left at its default false. If the application combines regex rules with a catch-all rule, the outcome is a rule mismatch rather than a fully public invocation.
candidates.root_cause: RegexRequestMatcher builds the match target from servletPath + pathInfo + queryString and evaluates it with pattern.matcher(url).matches() (web/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/web/util/matcher/RegexRequestMatcher.java:85-113). Patterns are compiled with only CASE_INSENSITIVE when requested and without DOTALL, and no rejection/normalization of CR/LF is performed (lines 66-75). In Java regex, '.' does not match line terminators by default, so a pattern such as "/admin/.*" evaluated with Matcher.matches() against a value containing a decoded newline (e.g. "/admin/secret\n") does not match the entire region. When the matcher returns false, DefaultFilterInvocationSecurityMetadataSource.getAttributes returns null (web/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/web/access/intercept/DefaultFilterInvocationSecurityMetadataSource.java:91-100), and AbstractSecurityInterceptor.beforeInvocation treats null/empty attributes as a public invocation, logging 'Public object - authentication not attempted' and returning without an access decision (core/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/access/intercept/AbstractSecurityInterceptor.java:199-216; rejectPublicInvocations defaults to false at line 121). The container can still resolve the same request to the protected path once the line terminator is normalized/stripped, producing a constraint bypass for applications that secure URLs solely with regex matchers and do not have a catch-all rule.
candidates.title: RegexRequestMatcher can fail to match URLs containing decoded line terminators, causing URL security constraints to be skipped
candidates.trace: Request URI with encoded/decoded CR/LF -> container populates getServletPath()/getPathInfo() -> RegexRequestMatcher.matches() concatenates servletPath+pathInfo (+queryString) (lines 91-106) and evaluates pattern.matcher(url).matches() (line 113) with a pattern compiled without DOTALL (lines 66-75) -> full-region match fails because '.' cannot consume the line terminator -> matcher returns false -> DefaultFilterInvocationSecurityMetadataSource.getAttributes() falls through its ordered map and returns null (lines 93-99) -> FilterSecurityInterceptor/AbstractSecurityInterceptor.beforeInvocation() sees null/empty attributes, treats the object as public, and proceeds without authorization (lines 199-216) -> container serves the protected resource for the normalized path.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed: the exact container behavior for line terminators in servletPath/pathInfo and the resulting end-to-end bypass were not executed. Not verified whether a specific released container surfaces decoded %0a/%0d in servletPath/pathInfo without rejecting the request, and not verified whether a trailing newline vs. embedded newline behaves identically for all '.'-based patterns. The behavior was reviewed on the default firewall (DefaultHttpFirewall), which likewise does not reject CR/LF.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization / pattern-matching bypass (regex semantics mismatch)

coverage_summary: get_source_scope reports 1340 model-visible files rooted at the assigned snapshot, no excluded/binary/symlinked files except that binary-like files are refused by the reader; the same filters apply to B0 and P1. I inspected modules acl, cas, config, core, crypto, data, ldap, messaging, oauth2 (core/client), openid, remoting, taglibs, web, webflux and samples at varying depth, prioritizing authentication, authorization, request matching, firewall, CSRF, session/remember-me, password encoding, ACL, LDAP/CAS/OpenID and OAuth2 code. Tests are absent from the snapshot (no **/src/test/** files), so behavior could not be cross-checked against repository tests. Coverage is targeted sampling plus several full-file reads, not a line-by-line audit of all 1340 files; large config classes, most samples/resources, and some lesser-used providers were skimmed rather than fully traced.
limitations: No execution, compilation, tests, or scanners were run (condition B0; read-only source review only).
The snapshot contains no test sources, so intended behavior could not be validated against the project's own tests.
Servlet-container behavior (decoding/normalization of %0a/%0d, '//', and path parameters) is not part of this repository and could not be inspected; exploitability of the candidate depends on it.
The container/version and application security configuration are unknown; the bypass path assumes regex rules without a later catch-all rule and rejectPublicInvocations left at its default false.

Candidate ranking is based on source evidence and impact, not on runtime confirmation; a different unfound issue may exist in areas that were only skimmed (large config builders, samples, remoting, some LDAP/OpenID branches).

rejected_leads.lead: Firewall path normalization (RequestWrapper.strip / DefaultHttpFirewall): tokenizing a path with a ';'-only segment yields an empty segment and leaves '//' in the result (web/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/web/firewall/RequestWrapper.java:87-110), contradicting its own javadoc; combined with a container that routes the normalized path to the protected resource, exact-path matchers could be skipped and the invocation treated as public.
rejected_leads.reason: Rejected as a second candidate because it is the same root cause class (path/pattern mismatch feeding null security attributes) and its exploitability depends on container-specific semicolon and duplicate-slash handling; on Tomcat path parameters are removed before the security filters, making it inert there. Kept as an unconfirmed lead, not a submitted candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultHttpFirewall / RequestWrapper as a whole is insufficiently strict compared with the later StrictHttpFirewall (encoded dots/backslashes/percent, semicolons, non-printable characters).
rejected_leads.reason: Broad hardening gap, not a demonstrated bypass: the class rejects un-normalized decoded paths and encoded slashes, and no container/servlet combination was traced in-repo to a concrete constraint bypass.

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultLoginPageGeneratingFilter writes the authentication exception message (session attribute WebAttributes.AUTHENTICATION_EXCEPTION) unescaped into the generated login page (DefaultLoginPageGeneratingFilter.java:191-218).
rejected_leads.reason: Attacker control of the message is not established for default providers (BadCredentialsException carries a fixed message; UsernameNotFoundException is hidden by default); would require a custom exception carrying user input, so it is an application-dependent hardening gap.

rejected_leads.lead: UserDetailsRepositoryAuthenticationManager compares the stored password with presented credentials via String.equals and no PasswordEncoder (core/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/authentication/UserDetailsRepositoryAuthenticationManager.java:41-45).
rejected_leads.reason: Plaintext-credential/design weakness in early reactive code, but it gives attacker-controlled input no way to bypass authentication in this snapshot; credentials must still equal the stored password.

rejected_leads.lead: ActiveDirectoryLdapAuthenticationProvider passes the unescaped bind principal into the LDAP search filter via SpringSecurityLdapTemplate.searchForSingleEntryInternal (parameters substituted by JNDI without LDAP filter escaping).
rejected_leads.reason: Filter injection is plausible but exploitation is limited: the same value is used for the LDAP bind, so valid credentials for that principal are still required, and no in-repo escalation path was traced.

rejected_leads.lead: Early OAuth2 client redirect/state handling (AuthorizationCodeAuthenticationProcessingFilter, AuthorizationCodeRequestRedirectFilter, HttpSessionAuthorizationRequestRepository, DefaultStateGenerator).
rejected_leads.reason: State is 32 random bytes stored server-side and compared before code exchange, and the returned redirect URI is compared with the stored authorization request; no missing attacker-exploitable check was found.

rejected_leads.lead: Miscellaneous spot checks that matched documented behavior: AntPathRequestMatcher, MediaTypeRequestMatcher, CsrfFilter/CookieCsrfTokenRepository, remember-me signature comparisons, session fixation strategies, BCrypt/PBKDF2/SCrypt encoders, AclEntryVoter/DefaultPermissionGrantingStrategy, webflux AuthorizationWebFilter/verify semantics, ExceptionTranslationFilter/AnonymousAuthenticationFilter.
rejected_leads.reason: Logic and constant-time/ordering protections were present and consistent with the classes' contracts; no attacker-controlled weakening identified.

summary: Assigned snapshot is the Spring Security multi-module tree (acl, cas, config, core, crypto, data, ldap, messaging, oauth2, openid, remoting, taglibs, web, webflux, samples) at version 5.0.0.BUILD-SNAPSHOT. I reviewed the central authentication/authorization paths (FilterChainProxy, AbstractSecurityInterceptor, FilterSecurityInterceptor, request matchers, firewall, CSRF, remember-me, session fixation, expression voters, method-security metadata, ACL voters, LDAP/CAS/OpenID providers, OAuth2 client, crypto/password encoders) and found the code largely coherent with its own contracts. The single strongest distinct candidate I can support from source is the authorization-bypass semantics of RegexRequestMatcher: it compiles the configured pattern without DOTALL/newline handling and applies full-region matching to a URL that can contain decoded line terminators, so a URL that a container routes to a protected resource can fail the matcher, yielding no ConfigAttributes and a public invocation. Supporting trace: when no RequestMatcher matches, DefaultFilterInvocationSecurityMetadataSource returns null, and AbstractSecurityInterceptor treats null/empty attributes as a public object (authentication is not attempted; rejectPublicInvocations defaults to false). This is a lead, not a runtime-confirmed finding; prerequisites and limitations are stated below.
